packet.headline_seed: Former Nigerian minister sentenced to 75 years in rare corruption verdict
packet.description_seed: Former Power Minister Saleh Mamman was convicted last week - but the authorities do not know his whereabouts.

what: Former Nigerian minister sentenced to 75 years in rare corruption verdict

clean_source_blocks.text: In an unprecedented ruling on Wednesday, a Nigerian court sentenced Saleh Mamman, the former minister of power, to 75 years in prison. The conviction was based on laundering charges involving 33.8 billion naira, approximately $24.71 million, brought forward by the nation's anti-graft agency. The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) revealed that the laundered funds, funneled through private companies, were linked to essential hydroelectric projects, including the significant Mambilla and Zungeru power plants. Justice James Omotosho delivered the verdict in Abuja, following a thorough examination of twelve charges against Mamman. This case throws the spotlight on Nigeria's ongoing battle against corruption among high-ranking officials, a chronic issue that affects the country's power infrastructure development amidst nationwide electricity shortages. Mamman, who served in 2019, is now a fugitive with a warrant for his arrest issued by Nigerian and international security age...
Former Power Minister Saleh Mamman was convicted last week - but the authorities do not know his whereabouts.

A Sentence That Shook the Corridors of PowerIn a ruling that reverberated across Nigeria's political and legal establishment, a Federal High Court in Abuja on Wednesday handed down one of the most severe corruption sentences ever imposed on a Nigerian government minister. The Federal High Court sitting in Abuja sentenced former Minister of Power, Saleh Mamman, to 75 years in prison for stealing public funds totaling about ₦33.8 billion. The conviction, delivered by Justice James Omotosho, brings to a dramatic close a case that laid bare the rot at the heart of Nigeria's perpetually troubled power sector and the brazen impunity of those entrusted to fix it.

Saleh Mamman, a former Nigerian power minister, has been sentenced to 75 years in prison for laundering 33.8bn naira ($24.7m; £18.5m), a rare conviction against corrupt officials in the West ​African nation. Last week, Mamman was found guilty of 12 counts, including using private firms to funnel money linked to government-funded power plants. The 68-year-old was sentenced in absentia on Wednesday - according to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Mamman has been "out of circulation" and "without trace" since his conviction. On Monday, the high court in the capital Abuja issued an arrest warrant for Mamman, who was power minister from 2015 to 2021. Mamman, who led the ministry of power under then President Muhammadu Buhari, has not publicly commented on his conviction.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Saleh Mamman, a former Nigerian power minister, has been sentenced to 75 years in prison for laundering 33.8bn naira ($24.7m; £18.5m), a rare conviction against corrupt officials in the West ​African nation.

Last week, Mamman was found guilty of 12 counts, including using private firms to funnel money linked to government-funded power plants.

The 68-year-old was sentenced in absentia on Wednesday - according to the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Mamman has been "out of circulation" and "without trace" since his conviction.

On Monday, the high court in the capital Abuja issued an arrest warrant for Mamman, who was power minister from 2015 to 2021.

Mamman, who led the ministry of power under then President Muhammadu Buhari, has not publicly commented on his conviction.

However just weeks before he was sentenced, the former minister announced plans to run for Taraba State governor in the 2027 elections, on behalf of Nigeria's ruling party.

"Today marks a defining moment in my journey of service to our dear state. With a deep sense of responsibility and unwavering commitment, I have officially obtained the Expression of Interest and Nomination Forms under the All Progressives Congress (APC) to contest for the governorship of Taraba State," he wrote on social media.

Mamman led the ministry of power at a time when President Muhammadu Buhari's administration had promised to tackle corruption.

Mamman was eventually sacked by Buhari in a cabinet reshuffle, after what the president called an "independent and critical self-review".

During Mamman's sentencing on Wednesday, the high court ordered him to repay 22bn naira ($16m; £12m).

The case is part of a wider anti-corruption drive targeting former government officials.

Other high-profile investigations by the EFCC have involved former Justice Minister Abubakar Malami and former Humanitarian Affairs Minister Sadiya Umar Farouq, who was recently declared wanted by the agency. They have both denied the allegations.

Mamman's conviction has reignited public anger over Nigeria's long-running electricity crisis – especially as the former minister had promised he would improve matters.

Despite being one of Africa's largest energy producers, Nigeria continues to face chronic power shortages, with frequent blackouts affecting homes and businesses across the country.

payload.title: Nigerian entiselle sähköministerille 75 vuoden vankeustuomio korruptiojutussa
payload.summary: Nigerian entinen sähköministeri Saleh Mamman on tuomittu 75 vuodeksi vankeuteen laajassa rahanpesu- ja korruptiojutussa. Viranomaisten mukaan hänen olinpaikkaansa ei kuitenkaan tiedetä.
payload.content:
Nigerian entinen sähköministeri Saleh Mamman on saanut 75 vuoden vankeustuomion poikkeuksellisen laajassa korruptiojutussa, joka liittyi 33,8 miljardin nairan eli noin 24,7 miljoonan dollarin rahanpesuun. Tuomio annettiin Abujassa sen jälkeen, kun Mamman oli todettu syylliseksi 12 syytekohtaan. Viranomaisten mukaan hänen olinpaikkaansa ei tällä hetkellä tiedetä.

## Tuomio annettiin poissaolevana

Mamman tuomittiin keskiviikkona poissaolevana. Nigerian talous- ja rahoitusrikoksia tutkivan EFCC-viraston mukaan hän on ollut tavoittamattomissa siitä lähtien, kun hänet todettiin syylliseksi viime viikolla. Abujassa toimiva korkea oikeus oli jo maanantaina antanut hänestä pidätysmääräyksen.

Oikeuden mukaan tapaus koski varoja, jotka oli kanavoitu yksityisten yritysten kautta. Rahojen kerrotaan liittyneen valtion rahoittamiin voimalaitoshankkeisiin. Lähdeaineiston mukaan jutussa mainitaan muun muassa Mambillan ja Zungerun vesivoimahankkeet, jotka ovat osa Nigerian pitkään ongelmissa ollutta sähkösektoria.

Mamman on 68-vuotias. Hän toimi sähköministerinä entisen presidentin Muhammadu Buharin hallinnossa vuosina 2015–2021. Hän ei ole lähdeaineiston mukaan kommentoinut tuomiotaan julkisesti.

## Harvinainen tuomio korkean tason virkamiehelle

Tuomiota on kuvattu harvinaiseksi Nigeriassa, jossa korkean tason korruptioepäilyt ovat usein herättäneet laajaa julkista huomiota mutta johtaneet harvemmin näin ankariin tuomioihin. Oikeus käsitteli Mammanin osalta useita rahanpesuun liittyviä syytekohtia, ja tuomion antoi tuomari James Omotosho.

Tapaus kytkeytyy laajempaan keskusteluun Nigerian julkisten varojen käytöstä ja erityisesti sähkösektorin kehittämisestä. Maa kärsii lähdeaineiston mukaan sähköpulasta, ja suurten energia- ja voimalaitoshankkeiden eteneminen on ollut osa laajempaa poliittista ja oikeudellista kiistaa. Mammanin tapaus nostaa esiin myös sen, miten valtion rahoittamiin hankkeisiin liittyvien varojen käyttöä valvotaan.

Viranomaisten seuraava keskeinen kysymys on Mammanin tavoittaminen. Koska tuomio annettiin hänen poissa ollessaan, rangaistuksen täytäntöönpano riippuu siitä, saadaanko hänet kiinni pidätysmääräyksen perusteella. EFCC:n mukaan Mamman on ollut ”jäljittämättömissä” tuomion jälkeen.
summary_bullets: Saleh Mamman tuomittiin 75 vuodeksi vankeuteen rahanpesu- ja korruptiojutussa.
Juttu koski 33,8 miljardin nairan varoja ja valtion voimalaitoshankkeita.
Nigerian viranomaiset eivät tiedä Mammanin olinpaikkaa, ja hänestä on annettu pidätysmääräys.
